nodes.name: Salt template annealing
nodes.procedure: In a typical synthesis of amorphous Mo/V-Ru NSs, 40 mg Ru(acac)3, 5 mg V(acac)3, 5 mg MoO2(acac)2 and 300 mg KBr were dissolved into 70 mL mixture containing ethanol and water (V_ethanol/V_DI water = 5/2). The mixture was dried to obtain the mixed powder, and then heated to 270°C for 90 min with a heating rate of 5°C min^-1 under air in a muffle furnace, and then naturally cooled to room temperature. As-obtained products were washed several times with the DI water/ethanol mixture.

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: To evaluate the alkaline HER performance, the Mo/V-Ru NSs and the control samples were loaded on the commercial carbon black, and tested them in Ar-saturated 1.0 M KOH solution at a rotating speed of 1600 rpm… The HER polarization curves display that the Mo/V-Ru NSs catalyst exhibits remarkably low overpotentials of 36 mV and 86 mV at current densities of 10 mA cm−2 and 100 mA cm−2… The Tafel slope of the Mo/V-Ru NSs catalyst is 37.1 mV dec⁻1

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images reveal nanosheet morphology with lateral dimensions exceeding 5 μm for Mo/V-Ru NSs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that Mo/V-Ru NSs exhibit an nanosheet morphology with lateral dimensions exceeding 5 μm (Figure 1a).

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing nanostructure with irregular morphology, textured surface features, and nanoscale dimensions
High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing thin, layered, translucent sheet-like structures with jagged edges and folds

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM confirms 2D feature with thickness of approximately 4.38 nm for Mo/V-Ru NS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 2D feature of Mo/V-Ru NSs can be further confirmed by the atomic force microscopy (AFM) image (Figure 1b) and the thickness of the Mo/V-Ru NS is evaluated to be approximately 4.38 nm (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD patterns verify amorphous structure with no detectable crystalline peaks for Ru NSs catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder X-ray diffraction patterns (PXRD) pattern verifies the Ru NSs catalysts are amorphous, showing no detectable crystalline peaks (Figure 1d).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows no discernible lattice fringes and SAED exhibits diffuse diffraction rings, confirming amorphous structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images exhibit the invisible discernible lattice fringes, and corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns exhibited diffuse diffraction rings (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS line scans and mappings reveal Ru, Mo and V are uniformly distributed across the nanosheet without obvious segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS line scans (Figure 1f) and mappings (Figure 1g) are employed to investigate the elemental distribution, revealing that Ru, Mo and V are uniformly distributed across the nanosheet without obvious segregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p XPS shows Ru predominantly in metallic state (Ru0) with positive shift upon Mo/V incorporation; Mo 3d shows Mo6+, Mo4+, Mo0; V 2p shows predominantly V3+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectra of Ru 3p reveal that Ru predominantly exists in the metallic state (Ru0)... High-resolution XPS spectra of Mo 3d reveal multiple valence states, including Mo6+, Mo4+, and metallic Mo0... the high-resolution XPS spectra of V 2p predominantly show V3+.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ FT-IR shows blue shift of 4.4 cm⁻¹ in H₂O bending vibration at ~1630 cm⁻¹ and enhanced intensity at low wavenumbers in H₂O stretching region (3000-3800 cm⁻¹) for Mo/V-Ru NSs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to pure Ru NSs, Mo/V-Ru NSs exhibit a blue shift of approximately 4.4 cm⁻¹ in the H₂O bending vibration peak at around 1630 cm⁻¹ (Figure 4a-b), indicating accelerated water molecule bending vibrations...

The double layer capacitance (Cdl) and ECSA of prepared catalysts: Mo/V-Ru NSs Cdl=138.45 mF cmgeo-2, ECSA=2307.50 cm2 cmgeo-2; Ru NSs Cdl=69.37 mF cmgeo-2, ECSA=1156.17 cm2 cmgeo-2.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows significantly lower charge transfer resistance Rct for Mo/V-Ru NSs compared to other Ru catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist diagram from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) shows a significantly lower charge transfer resistance (R_ct) compared to other Ru catalysts, highlighting the role of Mo and V in enhancing charge transfer kinetics (Figure 3c).
